notes: Derived edit. died_in carries chain:located_in->died_in, so dying on Saint Helena, in the South Atlantic, south of the equator, is dying in the Southern Hemisphere; a firm rule turns death in a hemisphere into died_in_hemisphere (functional). The South Atlantic's definition (P3) is firm. q1 compares hemispheres (fol).

queries.not_checked: fol: compares the hemispheres of two places (same hemisphere as Paris)

fol.notes: Places are an enumeration; the hemisphere of a place (in_hemisphere) and of Napoleon's death (died_in_hemisphere, functional) are uninterpreted functions to the two hemispheres, so the edit and the worlds can move them. The South Atlantic's definition (P3) and the rule from place of death to hemisphere of death are firm, as in the DL file. w2 moves Saint Helena north (its side fact).

local.in_hemisphere: in_hemisphere(x): the hemisphere (north or south of the equator) place x lies in; the functional value form of located_in to a hemisphere.

napoleon_st_helena.says: Napoleon Bonaparte died on Saint Helena. (premise)

st_helena_sa.says: Saint Helena is an island in the South Atlantic Ocean. (premise)

sa_south.says: The South Atlantic is the part of the Atlantic Ocean south of the equator: what lies in it is in the Southern Hemisphere.

hemisphere_rule.says: A person dies in the hemisphere of the place where they died.

paris_north.says: Paris is in the Northern Hemisphere. (stored)

label_corrections.why: 'Same hemisphere as Paris' over a functional link to one of two named hemispheres is a join through died_in_hemisphere and inv(located_in) restricted to Hemisphere; with northern and southern distinct and the relation functional it is expressible with nominals (napoleon : died_in_hemisphere some ({northern}) and paris : located_in value northern). No arithmetic.
